answer.origin: An NVIDIA representative told Tom’s Hardware on 2026-07-06, in the context of reports about the Kyber rack and Rubin Ultra roadmap, “Our roadmap is intact.” The publication date and stated date are both 2026-07-06.
answer.note: NVIDIA’s statement is a brief, official assertion that its roadmap remains intact, but it gives no product-specific clarification or schedule. It is relevant context for SemiAnalysis claims relayed by The Decoder that Kyber NVL144 was delayed by more than 12 months to 2028 due to PCB midplane problems (e49, e50), and that planned alternatives or configurations had been scrapped or changed (e51, e53). The general statement does not expressly deny those individual claims; a roadmap could remain intact while a product’s timing or configuration changes. Conditionally, it offers limited support for confidence in NVIDIA’s overall product plans, but does not establish shipment timing, customer deployments, or an effect on FY2027 Data Center revenue.
limitations: NVIDIA did not specify which products or milestones it meant by “roadmap,” or address the reported Kyber timing, NVL72x2, or Rubin Ultra changes individually.
The statement provides no product schedule, customer or shipment information, or revenue estimate with which to assess any FY2027 Data Center revenue impact.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA’s next official product-roadmap or earnings disclosures for a specific Kyber NVL144 schedule and clarification of whether the reported move to 2028 is accurate.
Check for NVIDIA confirmation or correction of the reported NVL72x2 and four-die Rubin Ultra status changes.
